title: The Borrowed Portrait Anew
premise: True-crime podcaster Quentin Nystrom has spent seven years documenting the unsolved disappearance of portrait artist Marguerite Voss, whose final painting vanished with her. A week after Quentin attends the funeral of the case's prime suspect, a confession letter arrives—postmarked the day after the burial—claiming the suspect was innocent and pointing Quentin toward a ledger of debts hidden inside the frames of Marguerite's surviving portraits. As Quentin traces the ledger's coded entries through the town's oldest families, they discover their own name among the debts, and that the letter's author is someone who faked a death to survive Marguerite's murder. The anniversary dinner of Marguerite's memorial society becomes a trap where the ledger's last entry is settled: Quentin exposes the killer—a respected patron who murdered Marguerite to erase what her portraits recorded—and chooses to publish the truth, finally belonging to the story instead of merely narrating it.
about_author: Jude Halloran is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales and unclaimed heirlooms before turning to fiction. Their mysteries are known for quiet menace, obsessive narrators, and objects that remember more than people do.

chapters.title: The Funeral I Wasn't Invited To
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Quentin's POV. Quentin attends Harold Breck's funeral uninvited, observing mourners for the podcast's final episode on Marguerite Voss. A stranger watches them from the back. Emotional beat: the hollow satisfaction of closing a case that never closed.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A confession letter arrives claiming Breck was innocent, with a hand-drawn key and the phrase 'count what hangs.' Quentin's producer urges them to drop it; Quentin can't. Emotional beat: the addictive dread of a door reopening.

chapters.title: Seven Portraits, One Missing
chapters.summary: Quentin visits the Voss estate sale remnants, cataloguing six surviving portraits while the seventh—the one that vanished—looms in every photograph. They notice faint pencil grids on stretcher bars. Emotional beat: wonder sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: The Memorial Society
chapters.summary: Quentin infiltrates a planning meeting for the annual Voss anniversary dinner, meeting patron Vivian Ashe and archivist Tomas Reyes. Everyone performs grief; no one performs it the same way. Emotional beat: belonging as camouflage.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Quentin decodes the first ledger entries: initials, dates, sums—payments spanning decades. The earliest predates Marguerite's disappearance by twenty years. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing the mystery is older than the crime.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin interviews elderly residents whose memories contradict the official timeline. One recalls Marguerite painting a portrait that was never displayed. That night, Quentin's studio is searched. Emotional beat: memory as contested territory.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Back
chapters.summary: Quentin tracks the funeral stranger to a motel under a dead man's name. The stranger, Dana Voss—Marguerite's niece, presumed drowned in 1999—slips away, leaving a second letter. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Faked Drowning
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Flashback to the night Marguerite died and why Dana let the river take her name. Present day: Dana watches Quentin, torn between using them and protecting them. Emotional beat: guilt as a lifelong tenant.

chapters.title: Debts of the Ascendant
chapters.summary: Quentin maps ledger names to town dynasties: the Ashes, the Pell family, the Brecks. Every portrait's subject owed or was owed. Vivian Ashe invites Quentin to dinner—too warmly. Emotional beat: hospitality with teeth.

chapters.title: The Grid on the Canvas
chapters.summary: Quentin photographs the portraits under raking light; the pencil grids form a coordinate cipher pointing to the Voss boathouse. Tomas catches them mid-theft and, instead of reporting, asks to help. Emotional beat: an alliance built on mutual hunger.

chapters.title: Boathouse at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Quentin and Tomas find a hidden panel: the seventh portrait, slashed but restorable, and Marguerite's journal. The portraits recorded blackmail—she painted what people confessed. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into danger.

chapters.title: Someone Else Is Reading
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The journal's later pages are torn out. Quentin realizes the podcast's early episodes tipped someone off—their own research lit the fuse. Emotional beat: complicity, the podcaster as accomplice.

chapters.title: Vivian's Table
chapters.summary: Dinner at the Ashe estate. Vivian probes with surgical courtesy; Quentin lies badly and learns Vivian's name appears in the ledger's final column—marked 'paid in full' the week Marguerite died. Emotional beat: a duel conducted in small talk.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Approaches
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. With the dinner days away, threats escalate: Tomas is attacked, Dana goes silent, and the podcast's sponsor pulls out under pressure. Emotional beat: isolation closing in like a tide.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Painted Last
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana reveals the torn pages: Marguerite's final entry named her killer and named Dana as witness. Dana fled, changed her face, and has spent twenty-five years being no one. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility, itemized.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Quentin and a conservator restore the slashed portrait overnight. Beneath the damage, Marguerite painted her killer's face into the background—half-finished, unmistakable to anyone who knows the town. Emotional beat: the dead testifying.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: The anniversary dinner. Quentin attends with the portrait photograph and the ledger, planning to expose the killer publicly. But Vivian pre-empts them, toasting 'the truth, however late,' and reveals she knows Quentin has the journal. Emotional beat: the trap springing shut.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Climax. Vivian confesses—not with remorse but with accounting: Marguerite's portraits threatened everything, and Breck took the blame willingly to protect his own ledger debts. Dana emerges as witness; Vivian's allies abandon her as the room turns. Emotional beat: justice arriving as arithmetic.

chapters.title: After the Toast
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Police, statements, fallout. Vivian, composed even in handcuffs, tells Quentin that publishing will cost them everything they've built. Quentin decides the story belongs to Marguerite and Dana, not to them. Emotional beat: the price of truth, accepted.

chapters.title: The Seventh Portrait Hung
chapters.summary: The restored portrait is hung in the town hall, Quentin's final episode airing as it's unveiled. Dana, under her real name at last, stands beside it. Emotional beat: restitution—of a painting, a name, a record.

chapters.title: What Belongs to the Story
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin ends the podcast, refusing a book deal that would exploit Dana. They keep one thing: Marguerite's pencil grid, framed. Emotional beat: belonging found by stepping out of the narrative's center.

chapters.title: A New Postmark
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Months later, an envelope arrives: no letter, only a small canvas swatch and a date—another town, another portrait, another ledger. Quentin packs a bag. Emotional beat: the past is never finished; neither is the work.
